assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new and highly tunable platform for flat-band, strongly correlated physics, with correlated insulators and gate-tunable superconductivity in a single carbon-based material. The idea of a controllable twist angle as a design parameter has generated moire quantum materials as a whole field. Originality and breadth are very high, and the effect is clean enough to be explained in a short citation.
assessment.attribution: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic angle (Bistritzer and MacDonald) and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity (Jarillo-Herrero group) are the decisive pair; early STM evidence of van Hove singularities at small twist angles (Andrei) is an earlier experimental contribution. A three-person configuration is possible but forces a choice between Bistritzer, Andrei and others; I give MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Andrei but regard Bistritzer's role as genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups reproduced the correlated phases and superconductivity within a few years, and the theoretical framework is well developed. Recognition after about eight years is timely, although the microscopic pairing mechanism is still debated.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unsettled.
Allocation among Bistritzer, MacDonald, Andrei and Jarillo-Herrero is not clean, and I am relying on memory of the historical record rather than verifying it.
Sample-to-sample variation in twist-angle disorder complicates reproducibility claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, together with the HgTe quantum-well demonstration, created a whole class of topological band-structure phases. It reshaped how condensed-matter physicists classify electronic matter and links to Majorana and topological quantum-computing ideas relevant for superconducting hybrid devices.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the original theoretical insight and Z2 classification; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realisation (with Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposing HgTe, who are not in the credited list). Hasan is credited for 3D materials, which is also important; with three slots I would choose Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, but the 3D realisation is a real competing claim.
assessment.maturity: The field has been confirmed by a large number of independent experiments, including ARPES on 3D materials and transport in 2D, and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: The exclusion of Hasan (3D topological insulators) and of the BHZ proposal makes the configuration contestable.
Quantised-edge-transport experiments in HgTe have shown imperfect quantisation, so the cleanest experimental confirmation is nuanced.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong light-matter coupling at microwave frequencies routine and became the architecture for superconducting quantum processors, dispersive readout and microwave quantum optics. The scientific content is both original and of lasting technical impact, and it underpins much of the field I work in.
assessment.attribution: Blais and co-workers proposed the architecture (with Schoelkopf's group), and the Wallraff-Schoelkopf experiments in 2004 demonstrated strong coupling. The three credited names are a plausible, reasonably clean configuration. Because I direct a quantum technology centre and have close collaborators in this area, I ought to be careful that my own proximity does not inflate the ranking.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many laboratories and now an industrial technology. However, the 2025 prize already honoured superconducting-circuit quantum effects, so recognition of closely related work so soon after may be seen as too concentrated, and I place it below candidates from other areas.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize may argue for waiting.
Credit among the Yale, Zurich and theory contributions (and earlier cavity-QED work by others such as Haroche, already honoured) needs care.
My own subfield makes my judgment potentially biased.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fractional statistics and anyons are a fundamental extension of the boson-fermion dichotomy in two dimensions and are central to topological quantum computing. The idea is deep and the experimental confirmation of fractional charge and anyonic braiding connects to quantum-information hardware.
assessment.attribution: Leinaas and Myrheim's 1977 work is the foundational theory of identical particles in low dimensions; experimental work on fractional charge and interferometric/collider evidence of anyonic statistics came from the Heiblum group and later from Fève and Manfra. Five names are credited, so any trio leaves out important contributors, particularly Fève and Manfra on the braiding experiments; Wilczek's separate role is not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Experimental evidence for anyonic statistics in the fractional quantum Hall regime has only recently become convincing (2020 onward) and is still being consolidated. Non-Abelian anyons remain unobserved. Recognition may be somewhat early for the experimental half, though the theory is old.
uncertainties: Which experiment constitutes the decisive confirmation is disputed.
Credit relative to Wilczek and Halperin, who are not on this candidate's list, cannot be assessed here.
Non-Abelian statistics, the part most relevant for quantum computing, is not established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantised conductance in quantum point contacts was a clean, textbook demonstration of ballistic mesoscopic transport and conductance quantisation in units of 2e^2/h. It launched much of semiconductor mesoscopic physics, and is the starting point for quantum-dot and gate-defined devices; I know this area well from my doctoral background in mesoscopic transport.
assessment.attribution: The 1988 papers of van Wees and colleagues (Delft/Philips) and of Wharam and colleagues (Cambridge) were independent and essentially simultaneous. Pepper was the senior figure at Cambridge; the credit among the Delft and Cambridge groups is fairly well defined, though other authors on those papers exist and Landauer's conceptual theory is not credited here.
assessment.maturity: The effect is thoroughly confirmed and understood, with decades of impact; recognition would be very late but not premature. Its tie to later Nobel-recognised mesoscopic topics is indirect.
uncertainties: The strong conceptual debt to Landauer-Buttiker theory is not credited.
Because the discovery is old, the committee may regard it as a lower-priority topic compared with more recent breakthroughs.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade enabled programmable neutral-atom arrays, which are now an important platform for quantum simulation and quantum computing with high-fidelity gates and large arrays. The work is original and has had rapid impact on the quantum-information landscape.
assessment.attribution: Lukin's group provided the blockade proposal and large programmable arrays; Browaeys' group demonstrated blockade and arrays of single atoms; Saffman contributed gate proposals and experiments. Zoller (also credited, with Jaksch and others) made the foundational proposals, so the choice of three necessarily excludes a very strong theoretical contributor.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by multiple groups, but the field is evolving very rapidly and error-corrected computing claims are still being established. The prize may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Whether the blockade proposal or the array demonstrations is the core discovery is unresolved.
The omission of Zoller from my choice may be disputed.
Platform maturity for computing remains uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposals of spin-qubit quantum computing in quantum dots and in silicon provided concrete blueprints for solid-state quantum computing and have led to working single- and two-qubit devices in silicon and germanium. The work is conceptually clear and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Loss and DiVincenzo (1998) proposed quantum-dot spin qubits; Kane (1998) proposed donor nuclear spins in silicon. These are distinct proposals that each led to a different technology line, so the three-person configuration is plausible but rests on proposals more than on a single experiment.
assessment.maturity: Experimental progress, particularly in silicon, has been strong, but the platform has not yet reached the scale of competing approaches, and the prize would honour a proposal whose full impact is still developing.
uncertainties: Theory proposals versus the experimental groups (Vandersypen, Morello, Dzurak and others, not credited here) raises attribution questions.
Platform scalability is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised the Hubbard model and quantum phase transitions in a controllable setting, and quantum-gas microscopes allow site-resolved observation. The approach established analogue quantum simulation as a practical research tool.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch and Zoller's proposal of the Bose-Hubbard model in lattices, Greiner, Bloch and Hansch's superfluid-Mott insulator observation, and Bloch's later work on microscopes and many-body physics are central. Credit among five listed names (including Cirac and Esslinger) is hard to compress into three.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed with many independent groups, but the most important simulation targets, such as the fermionic Hubbard model's d-wave phase, are not yet resolved, which suggests more development before recognition.
uncertainties: Hansch and Jaksch are not on the credited list, so the full intellectual history cannot be represented.
Whether the main discovery is the lattice implementation or the microscope is unclear.
